statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must have a French-language form; if the distinctive element is a foreign word or trademark such as 'Malatang', it must be romanized from Chinese script or be a recognized registered trademark under the Charter of the French Language; signage and commercial name must be predominantly French in the public workspace; Chinese characters may be used only as an auxiliary brand element after the French legal name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying Crown, government, or public authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file within 30 days a written request for administrative review with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, including the original reservation file number, alternative name analysis, and, where applicable, consent letters from professional bodies or trademark registrations; if the refusal is maintained, judicial review may be sought before the Court of Quebec in the district where the registered office is located.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2186 and 2236-2253 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 2, 13, 19-32; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar, REQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration for a Limited Partnership) executed by the general partner and filed with the REQ
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Québec société en commandite; limited partners' contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement and must be stated in the declaration, but no escrow account or minimum capital threshold is imposed by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the General Partner of the limited partnership (the Partnership): first, the subscriptions tendered by the initial Limited Partners to acquire Partnership interests, as recorded in the Partnership register, are hereby accepted, with contributions payable in cash within ten business days; second, the registered office is established at [full street address, postal code] in the Province of Québec; third, the General Partner shall file the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and appoint [Name] as authorized signing officer; fourth, the General Partner may open banking accounts, execute tax filings, lease premises and take all actions necessary to complete formation and obtain operating licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Partnership name clearance and distinctiveness verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online search services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ online register and conduct a keyword and distinctive-element search for the proposed partnership name, which must include the mandatory legal element S.E.C. (société en commandite) or L.P. If the desired name is not distinctive, file a Declaration of Name (Déclaration de nom) to reserve the name for 90 days. Verify that the general partner's own registration status is active before the declaration is submitted.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name incorporating S.E.C. or L.P. legal element
Certificate of name reservation or REQ search receipt, if applicable
Identification of the general partner with NEQ or date of birth
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ rejects the proposed name due to confusion with a prior registered name, select a new distinctive element and re-file the Declaration of Name; the REQ processes corrected re-filings within three business days with no additional fee for online resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of the limited partnership agreement and declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary or legal counsel, with subsequent REQ filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) under arts. 2236-2253 CCQ, specifying the general partner's identity, each limited partner's identity, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratio and management restrictions. Execute the agreement before a civil-law notary or by private deed with witnesses. Complete the REQ declaration of registration form, confirming the physical registered office address in Québec and the name and address of the general partner authorized to represent the partnership.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite)
Declaration of registration form completed for the REQ
Notarized or witnessed consent of the general partner
Proof of registered office address (lease, notarial deed or authorization letter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ returns the declaration as incomplete, use the online Régularisation module to amend the missing particulars within 30 days; ensure the general partner's consent is properly authenticated to avoid rejection of the registered office address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of declaration of registration and issuance of the Québec enterprise number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the declaration of registration electronically through the REQ online services portal, upload the executed partnership agreement for retention, and pay the CAD 82 registration fee by credit card or Interac. The REQ will issue the Québec enterprise number (NEQ) upon approval and publish the declaration in the register, making the limited partnership opposable to third parties as of the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Completed declaration of registration
Payment receipt for the registration fee
Executed partnership agreement for REQ retention
Mandate or power of attorney for the filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is suspended or refused, the REQ issues a notice of correction under s. 38 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; remedy the outstanding particulars within 15 days to avoid loss of retroactive effect against third parties and additional late-filing charges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax account registration with Revenu Québec and banking onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Schedule I chartered bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, file Form LM-1 with Revenu Québec to open the GST/HST (TPS) account, the QST (TVQ) account, and the employer source-deduction account if the partnership will have employees. Designate the general partner as the authorized representative. Simultaneously open the restaurant operating account and royalty wire account at a chartered bank, presenting the NEQ certificate, partnership agreement and a resolution of the general partner identifying the authorized signatories for local POS deposits and royalty wire transfers.
required_dossiers: NEQ registration certificate
Revenu Québec Form LM-1 (GST/HST and QST registration)
Executed partnership agreement and register of partners
General partner resolution appointing banking signatories
Identification documents for each signing officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec queries missing partner identification, such as a foreign limited partner's tax identification number, submit the foreign certificate of residence and update the REQ register; the tax accounts become effective as of the date of the complete submission, and voluntary registration can be backdated 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal commercial permit, fire safety approval and certificate of occupancy
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permits office (city or borough), Service de sécurité incendie, and Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) if tenant improvements are required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal commercial business permit application for the self-serve broth-bowl restaurant, attaching the layout plan, grease trap design, seating count and proposed kitchen exhaust system. Submit a fire safety inspection request to the municipal fire service and, if leasehold improvements alter the building envelope or egress, obtain an RBQ minor-work acknowledgment. After successful inspection, the municipality issues the certificate of occupation, which is a precondition for activating the MAPAQ restaurant permit.
required_dossiers: Commercial business permit application with layout plans
Fire safety inspection request and fire protection schematic
Certificate of occupancy application with load calculations
RBQ minor-work acknowledgment, if applicable
Lease or title deed for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality conditions approval on structural or ventilation changes, engage an engineer licensed in Québec to revise the plans and apply for re-inspection; any permit refusal may be appealed to the municipal permit review committee within 30 days of the written decision.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III - Exempt from a full environmental impact assessment under the Environment Quality Act, RLRQ c. Q-2, for a single-kitchen fast-casual restaurant discharging exclusively to municipal sewers; subject to municipal industrial wastewater authorization and, where the kitchen ventilation system exceeds local odour thresholds, a compliance attestation for the grease and odour abatement equipment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewers must not exceed 300 mg/L BOD5, 500 mg/L TSS and 100 mg/L oil and grease (the strictest municipal by-law prevails), and must pass through a certified grease interceptor sized per the National Plumbing Code of Canada 2020; kitchen exhaust must not create an odour nuisance beyond the property line and VOC concentrations must comply with municipal air-quality by-laws; used cooking oil must be stored in closed containers, removed by a registered waste hauler, and accompanied by disposal manifests retained for three years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local municipal fire safety service covering an automatic fire alarm system, a UL-300 suppression hood above the broth-cooking line, portable extinguishers and illuminated egress signage; Régie du bâtiment du Québec structural and electrical conformity for the dining area and kitchen; municipal certificate of occupation verifying occupant load, ventilation capacity, grease trap access and accessible washrooms; CNESST workplace health and safety registration with a prevention program addressing hot-liquid handling, sharp utensils, wet floor slip hazards and repetitive tasks in the self-serve serving area.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — GST/HST account and federal Business Number (BN); Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST) account and Québec business registration through Registraire des entreprises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign limited partnership must first obtain a federal BN by filing Form RC160 (GST/HST Application for Non-Resident) or via CRA My Business Account, and simultaneously register for the QST with Revenu Québec in the province of Québec, using the Registraire des entreprises enterprise number as the base identifier. Non-resident partners without fixed place of business may apply with a Canadian agent or address of record; documentary proof of the partnership deed and partner identification must be submitted; registrations are effective from the registration date or a specified earlier date if supply nexus exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No statutory check-the-box election exists in Canada; a Québec société en commandite (limited partnership) is automatically fiscally transparent for federal income tax and Québec tax purposes. Available elections include the GST/HST section 156 election for qualifying closely related corporations, annual vs quarterly filing elections, and a QST joint election with Revenu Québec for consolidated registration; partnerships may elect to classify activities as commercial under QST rules but cannot elect entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) administered federally at 5%; Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administered by Revenu Québec at 9.975%; Québec does not participate in the harmonized HST. The combined indirect tax burden is 14.975%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Québec within any four consecutive calendar quarters; for GST, CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada (other than certain excluded supplies) within the same four-calendar-quarter measure. If the limited partnership's domestic and foreign export turnover exceeds this threshold, mandatory registration applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal real-time tax clearance or fiscal stamping is required in Canada; CRA accepts electronic invoices if they remain legible and accessible. Québec has introduced a phased electronic-invoicing mandate for large businesses (including B2B transmissions via certified platforms), but there is no generalized API-based clearance or digital stamping for SME fast-casual franchise LPs. Invoices of a CA_LP should nevertheless comply with the required tax invoice content (BN, QST registration number, date, description, and GST/QST breakdown) and may be exchanged via EDI or Peppol-compliant networks when engaging with mandated counterparties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods qualifies for zero-rated GST/QST if the goods are physically exported by the supplier or on its behalf and the supplier obtains documentary evidence within the required statutory period. Export of franchise and royalty services to a non-resident franchisee is zero-rated when the service is supplied to a non-resident person, all or substantially all (90% or more) of the service is performed outside Canada, and the recipient is not registered for GST/QST in Canada. The CA_LP must be registered for GST/QST to claim refunds of input tax credits and to issue zero-rated invoices.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency CRI / Form B13 for non-CBSA systems)
Bill of Lading or Equivalent Transport Evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate or Bank Foreign Exchange Wire Record
Sales or Royalty Agreement with the Offshore Franchisee
Non-Resident Recipient Status Evidence (foreign GST/HST equivalency certificate, VAT registration certificate or signed declaration)
Packing List and Freight Forwarder Proof of Physical Export
Proof of Performance Outside Canada for Offshore Services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may disallow zero-rating and assess GST/QST on the full invoice amount plus interest if documentary export evidence is not produced on request. Penalties include GST/HST failure-to-file or false-statement penalties of 5% plus 1% per month and gross-negligence penalties up to 50% of understated tax; for Québec QST, similar recapture plus civil monetary penalties; deliberate evasion may be prosecuted as an offence, with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment; the same statutes contain a general six-year reassessment window for ordinary transactions and a ten-year window where misrepresentation occurs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential supervision of federally regulated banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and anti-money-laundering oversight by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada maintains no dedicated centralized foreign-exchange-control administration; exchange rate policy and payments-system oversight rest with the Bank of Canada, while the Minister of Finance retains residual authority under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a liberalized, fully convertible currency regime with no exchange controls, no prior-approval requirements, and no restrictions on current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance from a Quebec Limited Partnership to non-resident limited partners is unrestricted from an FX standpoint, but is subject to indirect fiscal frictions: Part XIII federal withholding tax and Quebec Taxation Act withholding on royalties, interest, and dividends paid to non-residents, reducible under the Canada-China Income Tax Convention (generally to 10% on royalties and interest). Additional non-FX frictions include FINTRAC reporting thresholds, CRS/FATCA self-certification obligations, and Quebec partnership allocation filings (Schedule TP-31/Relevé 15) for non-resident partners. No exchange-control permit or conversion license is required for capital injection, revenue repatriation, or trade financing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no statutory conversion timeline, and no required conversion ratio for foreign-currency receipts. Export and service proceeds may be retained at 100% in any freely convertible currency. For the Malatang master-franchise Limited Partnership, cross-border receipts such as franchise fees, royalties, and management fees may remain in USD, EUR, or CNY indefinitely, subject only to FINTRAC large-value transaction reporting and source-of-funds documentation at the receiving bank. Physical cross-border movement of currency or monetary instruments exceeding CAD 10,000 requires a CRA E677 report.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for receivables and payables clearing, LOW for capital escrow and statutory operating accounts. Canada does not recognize the EU/UK Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing class; non-bank payment providers must register as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and, in Quebec, must obtain a licence under the Act respecting money-services businesses administered by the Autorité des marchés financiers. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Ebury may legally settle inbound and outbound CAD cross-border flows as registered MSBs or foreign MSBs, but they cannot hold partnership capital in CDIC-insured accounts, cannot serve as the sole treasury bank for Quebec payroll or tax collection, and are not eligible for direct SWIFT membership or documentary-credit issuance. Recommended architecture confines EMIs to fast secondary rails for Chinese franchisee collections and China disbursements, while a Schedule I Canadian bank remains the primary system-of-record account holder.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec Limited Partnership with non-resident ownership, the six largest Canadian banks universally require an in-person or secure live-video KYC interview with at least one authorized signing officer of the General Partner. Complete digital-only onboarding is not offered for non-resident-connected partnerships under standard CDD policy, although FINTRAC permits compliant video identification where a notarized identity package and live verification are used. The bank will typically require a registered Quebec address as the record address, certified partnership resolutions, and a completed beneficial-ownership schedule. Passive limited partners need not appear personally provided the General Partner completes CDD and the ultimate-owner attestation is accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of indirect beneficial ownership where the Chinese master-licensor and non-resident limited partners sit behind the Limited Partnership capital waterfall
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed amended Limited Partnership Agreement with a per-tier beneficial ownership schedule; FINTRAC-compliant beneficial ownership attestation; notarized corporate organizational chart for the Chinese franchisor; passport copies and proof of identity for every holder of 25% or more; CRS self-certification (CRA Form RC591) and FATCA Form W-8BEN-E for each non-resident owner; registers of enterprises search showing no undisclosed security interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds red flag on a China-origin inbound capital injection exceeding the bank's CAD 50,000 to 100,000 internal threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chinese remitting bank advice evidencing lawful conversion and remittance through licensed PBOC-authorized channels; three years of tax-verified financial statements of the franchisor; SAFE/State Administration of Foreign Exchange filing for outward direct investment where applicable; executed master-franchise licensing agreement; escrow account statements; PPSA (Registre des droits personnels et réels mobiliers) search confirming no liens against the remitted funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hit or high-risk jurisdiction match triggered by the Chinese ultimate parent or franchise trademark
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening Match Explanation Memorandum with constituent-document proof; independent Dow Jones or World-Check name-screening report for all shareholders and directors; confirmation that the trademark and parties do not appear on the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Canadian Economic Sanctions Regulations lists, or OFAC SDN list; treasury workflow certification that automated dual-tier screening is applied to every cross-border payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) flag on any limited partner or on a beneficial owner of the Chinese franchisor entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed PEP Self-Declaration Form for every holder of 10% or more of the partnership; source-of-wealth evidence for any flagged individual, including salary records, business income tax returns, and divestiture documentation; independent World-Check or equivalent clearing letter; corporate resolution confirming no foreign political prominent person holds veto rights or control over LP disbursement mechanics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory-basis mismatch where the Malatang self-serve format lacks a visible Quebec food-establishment licence at the date of account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MAPAQ establishment licence application receipt and notarized food-processing plan; municipal commercial permit from the relevant Quebec municipality or borough; zoning clearance confirming self-serve broth-bar operations are a permitted fast-food use; Chinese food business license and food-safety production (SC) certificates for imported broth ingredients; signed commercial lease evidencing premises fitted with extraction-ventilation and self-serve stations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound franchise capital from China should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the Chinese parent's licensed bank to the Limited Partnership's segregated Operational Account with an explicit payment purpose code. Recommended statistical purpose codes follow Canada's Balance of Payments classification: use code 290 (charges for the use of intellectual property) for master-franchise licence-right injections, and classify pure intercompany equity funding as Foreign Direct Investment in Canada. No Bank of Canada or FX-administration approval is required, but the wire must clear OFAC and UN security filters, include complete remitter and beneficiary identifiers, and state a substantive purpose. Any single transfer at or above CAD 10,000 triggers FINTRAC large-value transaction reporting. For injections above CAD 2,000,000, a Canadian legal opinion confirming the funds are capital contributions rather than loans is advisable to avoid Part XIII interest withholding characterization. Physical import of monetary instruments exceeding CAD 10,000 requires a CRA E677 declarational filing. The bank's source-of-funds pack should retain the SAFE remittance voucher, notarized General Partner resolutions, and Chinese business licensing documents to prevent hold-funding delays.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Principal outbound disbursements are master-franchise royalty payments to the Chinese licensor and trade payments for imported broth powders, chili-based ingredients, and packaging equipment. Preferred clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for CAD-to-CNY royalty settlement through a Canadian bank's correspondent network or via Bank of China / ICBC New York branches, with the CAD/CNY leg optionally cleared through China's CIPS where the counterparty accepts participation; (2) irrevocable, confirmed at-sight documentary Letters of Credit issued by a Schedule I Canadian bank for bulk ingredient and equipment purchases, with commercial invoice, bill of lading, inspection certificates, and Chinese export-commodity inspection reports as the required document set; (3) bank-to-bank documentary collections (D/P or D/A terms) for smaller occasional batches; and (4) same-day domestic rails for intra-Quebec disbursements to franchisees using EFT or Interac-enabled corporate accounts. Outbound non-resident royalties must be flagged for withholding under the Quebec Taxation Act and federal Part XIII rules; to obtain the 10% Canada-China treaty rate, the payor should attach federal Form T626 and Quebec Form NR301/NR302 with the remittance and maintain a valid China-residency certificate from the Chinese State Taxation Administration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD spot and vanilla outright forward contracts (tenors up to 12 months) with a Schedule I Canadian bank for hedging inbound USD-denominated franchisee receipts and capital injections
CAD/CNH deliverable forwards transacted in the offshore CNH market through a Canadian licensed derivatives dealer to hedge royalty obligations and ingredient import costs
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on onshore CNY (USD/CNY and CAD/CNY) used when physical CNY delivery is unavailable, with notional settlement in CAD or USD
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/CNH) to match multi-year lease liabilities on kitchen, refrigeration, and extraction-ventilation equipment
Zero-cost FX option collars (call-and-put combinations) on CAD/USD and CAD/CNH limited to forecast royalty, franchise-fee, and import disbursements with no speculative intent

Exchange-traded commodity cross-currency hedges for imported food inputs such as vegetable oils and chili products, cleared through a Canadian derivatives dealer under the corporate end-user exemption

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), confirming the LP's general and limited partners, registered office, and business activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Government of Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through March 31; hard statutory deadline March 31; government fee is approximately CAD $38 (USD 28 at prevailing exchange)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers the REQ administrative late-fee tariff; non-filing for three consecutive years exposes the LP to administrative strike-off (radiation d'office). During delinquency the partnership loses legal publicity, preventing the LP from asserting its limited-liability shield against third parties; penal fines ranging from CAD $500 to $4,500 may be imposed on the LP and its general partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada federal partnership information return (T5013) and T5013 partnership income slips issued to each partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due May 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD $25 per day (minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $2,500); separate per-slip penalties of CAD $100 to $250 for late or incorrect T5013 slips; habitual non-filers may face additional penalties equal to 10% of gross revenue and criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec partnership information return (TP-600) and annual slip reporting to Québec partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the partnership fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD $25 per day (minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $2,500); Revenu Québec may also assess penal interest of 1.53% per month compounded on any balance payable and deny deduction or credit claims until the return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST return and Québec Sales Tax (QST) return covering taxable consideration received under master franchise and royalty agreements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST) and Revenu Québec (QST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One month after the end of the reporting period; for a December 31 fiscal year-end on annual filing, due January 31 of the following year; monthly filers remit by the last day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty of 5% of net tax due plus 3% on the second month and prescribed daily interest; Revenu Québec imposes a 5% penalty plus 1.53% monthly compounded interest and may suspend input tax refunds until all outstanding QST returns are filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer annual T4 slips and T4 Summary (CRA) and Relevé 1 (RL-1) slips and RLZ-1.S Summary (Revenu Québec) for the LP's Québec payroll
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the last day of February immediately following the calendar year (February 28 or February 29 in leap years)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA penalty of CAD $25 per day per late return (minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $2,500); Revenu Québec applies comparable administrative fines and 1.53% monthly penal interest on unremitted source deductions; repeated defaults may trigger payroll source-withholding audits and director/general partner liability assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the register of individuals with significant control (RISC), including updates reflecting any transfers of limited partnership units during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory records; verified and synchronized with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec annual declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed by March 31 in line with the REQ annual declaration; internal RISC updates due within 30 days of any change of significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or confirm the RISC constitutes a penal offence under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, punishable by fines up to CAD $4,500 for the enterprise; non-compliant LPs are also exposed to REQ strike-off and loss of opposability of limited partnership status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit is imposed on a Québec limited partnership by the Civil Code of Québec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An independent audit becomes mandatory only if (a) the partnership agreement or a unitholder resolution requires it; (b) the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation subject to NI 51-102 annual audit requirements; (c) CRA or Revenu Québec issues a statutory written demand for audited financial statements; or (d) a secured lender, franchisee agreement, or master licence contract imposes an audit covenant. For a fast-casual franchisor LP, reviewed or audited financial statements are commercially typical to satisfy franchise disclosure expectations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook – Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the governing framework for a private non-listed Québec LP; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is mandatory if the LP or its partners are publicly accountable or reporting issuers. CRA and Revenu Québec accept ASPE-prepared financial statements for income measurement, GST/HST, and QST purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Québec Bill 78 amendments to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the LP must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (RISC) showing every individual holding 25% or more of partnership units or controlling the LP by any other means, together with name, domicile, service address, and control date. The RISC is updated within 30 days of any triggering event, including any transfer of limited partnership units. The REQ annual declaration confirms the RISC content; where no individual has significant control, the LP must expressly record and declare that fact. Failure to confirm or update RISC data in the annual declaration is a penal offence separate from any tax liability.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of individuals with significant control (RISC) of the limited partnership
Register of general and limited partners with unit ownership and transfer history supporting the REQ annual declaration
Minute book of partnership resolutions (admissions, withdrawals, amendments, and annual consents) kept by the general partner
Partnership agreement, declaration of registration, and all amendment documents kept at the registered office in Québec

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - 1,150 per year (CAD 600 - 1,500) for third-party registered-office or registered-agent coverage in Québec, including REQ annual declaration administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No audit statutorily required; a notice-to-reader engagement by a Québec CPA firm typically ranges USD 2,200 - 6,500 (CAD 3,000 - 9,000); a full audit of a fast-casual franchisor LP with master licensing typically ranges USD 11,000 - 25,000 (CAD 15,000 - 35,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15% + Quebec provincial 11.5% for general corporate income; note: Limited Partnership is a pass-through entity, income taxed at partner level)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions for partnerships; partners may claim applicable deductions (e.g., small business deduction if partner is a CCPC, but not at partnership level). Active business income may be eligible for the federal small business deduction if allocated to a Canadian-controlled private corporation partner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 - Partnership Information Return (federal) filed via CRA's e-file (EFILE) or NETFILE; Quebec equivalent is the CO-17 - Partnership Information Return filed via Revenu Québec's online portal (clicSÉQUR).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., June 15 for a December 31 year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source business income; non-resident partners must file a Canadian tax return if they have a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses (cost of goods sold, operating expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses must be reasonable and supported by documentation; non-residents must ensure expenses are attributable to Canadian-source income.
Allocated to partners based on partnership agreement; non-resident partners are subject to Canadian tax on their share of income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income to partners (name, address, share percentage)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full details of non-resident partners; they may be subject to Part XIII withholding on certain payments (e.g., interest, royalties) but not on profit distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 per day up to CAD 2,500 for T5013; additional penalties for gross negligence (up to 50% of tax payable). For Quebec, similar penalties under the Taxation Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for partnership distributions (pass-through entity); if the entity were a corporation, the statutory rate is 25% for non-resident shareholders, reduced by tax treaties (e.g., 5% for substantial shareholding under Canada-US treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, non-resident partners must submit Form NR301 (Canada) or equivalent to the CRA, along with a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their home tax authority. The TRC must be issued within 3 years of the claim. For Quebec, a separate application may be required via Revenu Québec.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% (federal), reduced to 10% under most treaties (e.g., US, UK). Interest: statutory 25%, but often exempt under treaties (e.g., 0% for arm's length interest under US treaty). Quebec imposes an additional 12% provincial withholding on royalties and interest, but treaty relief may apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if cross-border transactions with non-arm's length parties exceed CAD 1 million for goods, CAD 500,000 for services, or CAD 250,000 for other transactions. Master File required if total annual revenue exceeds CAD 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Section 245 of the Income Tax Act applies. The CRA may challenge transactions lacking economic substance, and the partnership must demonstrate real business purpose and substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or deliberate misrepresentation of partnership income in tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act (Section 239) with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil penalties of 50% of the understated tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and partners may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in the evasion; travel bans may be imposed under the Canada Revenue Agency's enforcement powers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a limited partnership without real business activity, employees, or physical presence in Quebec, solely to obtain tax benefits or avoid reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess the partnership and deny deductions, impose penalties under GAAR (Section 245) of up to 50% of the tax benefit, and potentially reclassify the entity as a corporation for tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners may be personally liable for the partnership's tax debts if the partnership is deemed a sham; directors of corporate general partners may face civil restitution and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a money services business (if applicable), inadequate record-keeping of large cash transactions (over CAD 10,000), or failure to report suspicious transactions to FINTRAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million for individuals and CAD 2 million for entities per violation; criminal penalties for willful non-compliance include imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and partners can be held personally liable for fines if they knowingly failed to implement AML controls; travel bans may be issued under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
